name: HomeCoin
oneLiner: HOME is HomeCoin's dollar stablecoin backed by U.S. home-loan liens and property receivables, with foreclosure as the ultimate recovery path.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Possible retained: reviewed metadata indicates direct token, vault, issuer, pause, proxy, or admin-control uncertainty, but available registry sources do not prove an active holder-balance blacklist path.

collateral: U.S. home-loan liens and property-backed receivables originated through the HomeCoin/Bacon lending process
pegMechanism: Users fund property-backed loans with stablecoins; loans are secured by recorded liens and nonpayment can lead to foreclosure or sale proceeds

reserves.name: U.S. home loan liens / property-backed receivables

notices.title: Illiquid RWA collateral
notices.message: HomeCoin collateral is property-backed receivables, so the fallback is not comparable to liquid fiat or Treasury redemption capacity.

mintAuthority.summary: HOME is minted by Bacon Protocol 'Pan' smart contracts when a borrower draws an overcollateralized loan against a recorded property lien (ERC-721); BACON governance can add Pans and licensed servicers originate the underlying loans.

controls.label: Bacon Protocol Pan lending/mint contract
controls.capDescription: HOME supply expands only as new overcollateralized home loans are originated through a Pan; minting is tied to lien-backed loan creation rather than free issuer mint.
controls.evidence: Bacon Protocol docs describe 'Pans' as the core lending contracts that pool funds and mint HOME when a homeowner takes a lien-backed loan; supply is uncapped and demand-driven, not minted at issuer discretion.

controls.label: BACON governance / licensed servicers
controls.evidence: BACON is the governance token able to add new Pans and tune loan criteria; licensed servicers/LoanSnap originate and service the loans, gating which liens can mint HOME.

review.evidence: Project materials describe collateralized mint: HOME is created by Pan contracts at loan origination against recorded property liens, with BACON governance over Pan parameters and licensed servicers originating loans. No central issuer-discretion mint path is described.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the on-chain Pan/minter contract address and any owner/proxy admin on Ethereum, and confirm whether HOME minting can be triggered outside the loan-origination path.
Confirm current BACON governance scope and whether servicer onboarding is fully decentralized or admin-gated.
